passages.context: The complete poem was read in the exact hashed Gutenberg delivery, lines 7057-7193. Especially relevant are lines 7085-7110: the speaker blesses and praises divine might for making him a chosen sample and a pillar in the temple, then turns to his own misconduct. The poem structurally echoes the Pharisee's self-congratulating prayer and redirects it into satirical exposure; it does not quote the appointed Douay-Rheims wording exactly.

work.description: Robert Burns's 1785 satirical dramatic monologue in the voice of William Fisher, whose self-congratulation, claimed election, excuses, and curses turn the Pharisee's posture into an exposure of religious hypocrisy.
